*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for LUTs for 9-corner ($2^9$ entries) and 13-corner ($2^{13}$ entries) cells.
The size of these LUTs is larger than those for regular cells, but they are pre-computed and static.
*   **Strengths:** Significantly reduces triangle count and rendering time compared to uniform contouring while preserving visual details.
*   **Limitations:** Performance is still dominated by uniform contouring, limiting the speedup for very high-resolution data.
*   **When to Use:** When interactive rendering of large volumetric datasets is required and the viewer position changes frequently.
It is suitable when visual detail can be sacrificed at a distance without noticeable quality loss.

*   **When Not to Use:** When the viewer is always close to the object (where uniform resolution is needed) or when the overhead of managing transition cells outweighs the benefits (e.g., very small datasets).
